source.title: Interpreting CLIP with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Vladimir Zaigrajew; Hubert Baniecki; P. Biecek

record.tranche_reason: Appendix H measures stability of SAE feature directions across training seeds, bearing on seed convergence (V3) using a different metric from direct representation-alignment measurements.
record.gate_note: The seed-stability results in Appendix H bear on V3. The paper’s CKNNA results compare SAE activations with their input embeddings, not independently trained vision and language models; they do not test cross-modal convergence or representation interchangeability. Concept counts and examples do not measure whether universal features recur across different models.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE-method paper on CLIP embeddings. It uses CKNNA, the PRH alignment metric, only as a tool to score how well SAE activations preserve CLIP embedding neighbourhoods. The Appendix H seed-stability result measures whether sparse autoencoder dictionaries, trained on fixed CLIP embeddings, recover the same directions across seeds. It does not measure whether the networks being studied learn shared representations across initializations. It reports no random or chance reference, and the authors do not frame it as evidence about convergent learning. It is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only Appendix H. The paper's main conclusion is that Matryoshka SAE achieves a better sparsity–fidelity Pareto frontier than ReLU, TopK and BatchTopK SAEs on CLIP. It reports about 0.99 cosine similarity, under 0.1 FVU and about 80% sparsity. MSAE also yields over 120 validated concepts usable for similarity search and bias analysis. In Appendix H, stability correlates with sparsity and MSAE's stability trade-off is on par with other SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: Measures stability of SAE encoder and decoder directions across training seeds; it does not reproduce the original representation-convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that the reported stability metric is highly correlated with sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs with expansion rate 8 on CLIP ViT-L/14 embeddings show partial recovery of the same decoder and encoder directions across training seeds. Decoder stability is about .20–.69 and encoder stability about .04–.25. Stability is highly correlated with sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse autoencoder dictionaries trained on the same embeddings from different seeds recover only partly overlapping features, and overlap rises with sparsity.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The relevant stability table gives no uncertainty estimates or stated reference threshold for interpreting the values as shared features. The reported results cover CLIP ViT-L/14 SAEs at expansion rate 8 and do not directly demonstrate recurring features or shared subspaces.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results, including reconstruction fidelity, CKNNA between SAE activations and CLIP embeddings, concept counts, and concept-manipulation demonstrations, were left out because they do not measure the claim versions tested here.

untested.parts: All: no comparison of independently trained models across scale.
All: no vision-versus-language model alignment. CKNNA compares SAE activations with their own input embeddings.
No measurement of base networks trained from different seeds. Only SAE dictionaries trained on fixed embeddings are compared across seeds.
All: no mapping or stitching between models.
All: concepts are named within one CLIP model's SAEs, not matched across models.

missing.what: BatchTopK (k=64) stability row, .586/.238 (decoder/encoder). Omitted from the rows.

record.verdict_notes: CKNNA (from the Platonic Representation Hypothesis) is used only as an SAE-quality metric between SAE activations and CLIP embeddings, which is a T4 use. The seed-stability table reports no uncertainty and no random-direction baseline, so its values cannot be read as convergence evidence even for SAEs.

versions.untested_parts: Scale- and capability-related convergence between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data.
Alignment between vision and language model representations of paired images and captions as both models improve.

The study measures a seed-stability metric for SAE directions, but does not establish that many of the same features or shared subspaces recur, or distinguish shared features from shared individual units or bases.
Mapping representations between models, stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
Whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across different models.
Whether convergence changes with similarity-measure settings or input data, or disappears out of distribution.
Whether alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or is explained by shared data or objectives.

reader_labels.condition: Tested SAE variants at expansion rate 8 on CLIP ViT-L/14, ImageNet-1k
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that stability correlates strongly with sparsity and describe MSAE’s stability trade-off as on par with alternatives, so the result is conditional on the sparsity–reconstruction trade-off rather than evidence of uniformly shared features; see r1–r15.
